data.text/markdown: In this tutorial we show how to use our package to verify projected gradient descent for the nonnegative least-squares problem: ||[\begin{array}{ll} \text{minimize} & (1/2) \lVert Az - x \rVert^2 \\ \text{subject to} & z \ge 0, \end{array}||]where ||(A \in {\bf R}^{m \times n}||), ||(m \ge n||), ||(z \in {\bf R}^n||) is the decision variable, and ||(x \in {\bf R}^m||) parameterizes the family of problems. For the first order method, we choose projected gradient descent with step size ||(\eta > 0||), with iterates given by ||[\begin{array}{ll} z^{k+1} = {\bf ReLU}(z^{k} - \eta A^T(Az^{k} - x)), \end{array}||]where ||(\bf ReLU(v) = \max\{v, 0\}||) element-wise.

In this example, we choose ||(m = 5, n = 3||), randomly sample ||(A||), and parameterize ||(x||) as a unit box. We also choose ||(\eta = 1/L||), where ||(L||) is the maximum eigenvalue of ||(A^T A||). We initialize the algorithm with ||(z^0 = 0||).

We first simulate the algorithms on given problem instances, which are parameterized by the set of parameters ||(x \in \mathcal{X} = [x_{\text{lb}}, x_{\text{ub}}]||). We randomly sample ||(x||) from uniform distribution over ||(\mathcal{X}||). The output of VP.solve(K=K) will be an array of size (n_samples, K) whose ||(n||)-th row is a list of infinity norm of residuals z[k] - z[k-1] for k=1,...,K. After VP.solve method has run, the Verifier class provides statistics of the residual at last iterate z[K].
